chapters.name: Computation realization graph
chapters.title: Make computation physically real
chapters.summary: A computation becomes a machine through representations, interfaces, constraints and evidence.
chapters.question: What must remain true as an abstract computation crosses into silicon and a working system?
chapters.read: The graph is a causal teaching model: each boundary carries state, timing, energy, error and verification obligations. It is not a proprietary chip floorplan or a claim that one universal implementation exists.

chapters.name: Closure and operating proof
chapters.title: Close the chain
chapters.summary: Design is complete only when the physical system preserves the computation under real constraints.
chapters.question: How do we know a physical implementation still performs the intended computation?
chapters.read: The final graph keeps chip design, package integration, runtime behavior and acceptance evidence in one loop. A passing simulation is one gate; qualification and useful workload evidence are additional gates.

lessons.name: The computation-to-realization gap
lessons.role: Defines the problem of carrying a computational intent into a physically constrained machine.
lessons.description: An algorithm can be specified as a function over symbols, tensors or state transitions without saying how a device will store, move, time or verify those states. Realization begins when that specification is given a representation, an architecture, interfaces and measurable acceptance conditions. The same computation can be realized by different circuits and systems, each with different communication, energy, fault and manufacturing boundaries. This lesson makes the gap explicit so the later chip-design steps are understood as transformations of a contract rather than an unexplained jump from software to a finished die.

specs.label: Boundary
specs.context: A teaching boundary; no single implementation is implied.

specs.label: Required invariants
specs.value: Meaning, timing, energy, error and interface scope
specs.context: Each invariant needs a measurable definition before signoff.

interfaces.name: Computation intent
interfaces.signal: Function, tensor graph, state transitions and quality target

interfaces.name: Realization contract
interfaces.signal: Representations, interfaces, budgets and proof obligations

lessons.tradeoff: More detailed contracts reduce ambiguity but increase design and verification effort; an underspecified contract moves risk downstream.
lessons.whyAI: AI systems are useful only when model operations survive the chain into memory, arithmetic, communication, power, cooling and evaluation.

sources.title: Semi AI Foundry — Communication Theory of Computation Realization

lessons.scale: Abstract state to physical system; representation boundaries
mechanism: State the computation independently of a particular chip implementation.
Choose physical representations with defined noise, timing and energy margins.
Carry those representations through architecture, design, manufacturing and operation.
Measure whether each boundary preserves the required behavior.
Feed failures back into the next design or deployment decision.
lessons.misconception: A high-level algorithm is not a chip design; realization adds interfaces, budgets, implementation choices and evidence.

check.question: What makes an abstract computation physically realizable?
options: Naming a semiconductor process alone
A chain of representations and verified interfaces that preserve its required behavior
Increasing parameter count until a circuit appears
check.explanation: Realization is a chain of constrained transformations and checks, not a single process-node label.

science.title: A realization contract
science.explanation: A useful contract records representation R, interfaces I, budgets B, error model E and verification evidence V. The tuple is a design scaffold, not a theorem that all systems share one format.
science.assumptions: The tuple is a conceptual decomposition; each element must be instantiated for a chosen workload and physical boundary.

lessons.learningObjective: Explain why an abstract computation needs a typed, measurable path into a physical machine.
lessons.engineeringExample: Trace a matrix multiply from its graph operation to a tile schedule. The operation is unchanged, but layout, data type, memory traffic, arithmetic units, link budgets and acceptance tests become explicit at each boundary.
lessons.evidenceNotes: This lesson presents the CRG framing as Semi AI Foundry research context and separates it from the independently sourced physical-computation literature.

lessons.name: Communication is the realization medium
lessons.role: Maps computational state, data movement and control into a graph of physical interfaces.
lessons.description: Every physical implementation communicates: gates exchange signals, memories exchange addresses and data, dies exchange packets, and systems exchange work and checkpoints. The computation-realization graph treats these transfers as first-class objects with source, destination, encoding, rate, latency, energy and error conditions. This makes data movement visible beside arithmetic. It also explains why communication theory is useful to chip design: a representation is only operational when a receiver can distinguish it within the available noise, timing and power margins. The graph can be refined from a conceptual edge to a routed wire or protocol transaction without changing its teaching role.

specs.label: Edge fields
specs.value: Payload, encoding, rate, latency, energy, error
specs.context: Values require a declared boundary and time period.

specs.label: Node fields
specs.context: A node may be logical or physical; the model labels the abstraction.

interfaces.name: State receiver
interfaces.signal: Accepted data with timing and error conditions

lessons.tradeoff: More communication can improve locality or redundancy while increasing wires, buffers, power and verification surface.
lessons.whyAI: Attention, all-reduce, KV-cache traffic and checkpointing are communication graphs whose edges can bind an AI system before arithmetic does.

sources.title: Semi AI Foundry — Communication Theory of Computation Realization
Claude Shannon — A Mathematical Theory of Communication

lessons.scale: Signal, wire, link, fabric and workload graph
mechanism: Represent a computational dependency as a producer-to-consumer edge.
Assign an encoding and distinguishability condition to the edge.
Add rate, latency, energy and error budgets at the chosen boundary.
Map logical edges to physical paths, buffers, interfaces and protocols.
Measure delivered useful information rather than nominal link capacity.
lessons.misconception: A link labeled high bandwidth does not guarantee useful workload throughput when latency, contention, serialization or receiver capacity binds.

check.question: Why does the CRG include communication beside computation?
options: Because arithmetic never consumes energy
Because physical states must be transferred and distinguished between operations
Because all chips use the same network topology
check.explanation: The receiver and the path are part of a physical implementation of a computation.

science.title: A communication edge
science.explanation: A simple edge model separates startup latency α from payload transfer M/β and scales energy with transferred bits and an effective energy-per-bit term.
science.assumptions: Homogeneous effective bandwidth and energy; protocol overhead, contention and topology require additional terms.

lessons.learningObjective: Draw a communication edge with a payload, receiver, timing boundary and error condition.
lessons.engineeringExample: For a 1 GB collective payload over a 100 GB/s effective path with 5 μs startup, the payload term is about 10 ms; a topology or contention change can dominate the same arithmetic operation.
lessons.evidenceNotes: The edge equation is a bounded teaching model. Shannon’s source addresses communication limits; it does not by itself specify a chip architecture.

lessons.name: Architecture is a contract between computation and silicon
lessons.role: Chooses execution, memory and communication structures that can satisfy a workload contract.
lessons.description: Architecture turns a computation graph into a repeatable organization of execution units, storage levels, interconnects and control. A CPU, GPU, TPU, FPGA, NPU or wafer-scale array realizes similar mathematical operations through different communication patterns and scheduling rules. The CRG view asks which state is retained, where it moves, who controls it, and what happens when a path is full or a unit fails. Architecture is therefore a contract: software assumes a set of behaviors, while implementation must satisfy those behaviors within power, area, timing, test and manufacturing limits.

specs.label: Contract axes
specs.context: A comparison must use the same workload and boundary.

specs.label: Unknowns
specs.context: Public architecture claims are not reverse-engineered geometry.

interfaces.name: Implementation plan
interfaces.signal: Units, memory hierarchy, links, schedules and budgets

lessons.tradeoff: More specialization can improve efficiency for a stable graph while reducing flexibility and increasing software or qualification effort.
lessons.whyAI: The architecture determines whether model-scale tensor traffic becomes useful work or a queue of waiting memory and communication requests.
lessons.scale: Graph, architecture, tile and memory hierarchy
mechanism: Extract operator shapes, precision, reuse and synchronization from the workload.
Choose an execution model and dataflow that expose useful parallelism.
Allocate registers, local storage, shared memory and external memory roles.
Specify communication, ordering, fault and recovery behaviors.
Pass the contract to the compiler, RTL and physical-design teams.
lessons.misconception: An architecture label does not determine workload performance without a compiler path, memory behavior, topology and operating boundary.

check.question: What does the architecture contract connect?
options: Only the transistor count and logo
The workload’s required state transitions with execution, storage and communication behavior
Only a benchmark score
check.explanation: Architecture defines how the computation can be carried by a machine under its physical and software constraints.

science.title: Workload-bound rate
science.explanation: A simple bound compares arithmetic capacity with memory and network delivery capacity after expressing each as a compatible workload rate.
science.assumptions: Peak terms, arithmetic intensity and network intensity share a precision, batch and time boundary.

lessons.learningObjective: Compare two architectures by execution model, memory path and communication behavior rather than by a single peak number.
lessons.engineeringExample: A tensor kernel with low arithmetic intensity may remain memory-bound on a larger accelerator. Changing tile reuse or placing data closer to the unit can raise useful rate without changing the mathematical graph.
lessons.evidenceNotes: The bound is a roofline-style teaching model. Public architecture documentation supplies examples, not a universal product ranking.

lessons.name: From architecture contract to a chip
lessons.role: Traverses specification, RTL, verification, synthesis, physical design, tapeout and wafer test.
lessons.description: A chip design is a sequence of constrained transformations. The architecture contract becomes microarchitecture and RTL, then a verified netlist, a placed-and-routed layout, mask data and a process-specific tapeout. The PDK supplies rules and models; timing, power, signal integrity, design-for-test and manufacturability gates prevent an attractive logical design from becoming an untestable or unbuildable die. The CRG makes communication explicit at every handoff: module interfaces, clock and power domains, floorplan distances, package bumps and external links all carry obligations that must survive the transformation.

specs.label: Design chain
specs.value: Spec → microarchitecture → RTL → netlist → layout → tapeout
specs.context: A representative flow; organizations partition responsibilities differently.

specs.label: Closure gates
specs.value: Functional, timing, power, DFT, physical and manufacturability
specs.context: Passing one gate does not imply the others pass.

interfaces.name: Architecture contract
interfaces.signal: Behavior, interfaces, budgets and verification targets

interfaces.name: Tapeout package
interfaces.signal: Mask data, signoff evidence and test structures

lessons.tradeoff: More margin and redundancy can improve yield or reliability while consuming area, power, schedule and mask complexity.
lessons.whyAI: The models and kernels that drive AI systems become useful only when their numerical and communication assumptions are realized in a qualified chip and package.

sources.title: Semi AI Foundry — Communication Theory of Computation Realization
imec — CMOS scaling and system co-optimization

mechanism: Refine the architecture contract into clocked state, interfaces and microarchitectural resources.
Verify behavior and synthesize the design using process-specific libraries and models.
Place, route and close timing, power, signal integrity, DFT and physical rules.
Generate masks and send a reviewed tapeout to the chosen foundry process.
Probe, bin and feed measured results back into the design and architecture loop.
lessons.misconception: Tapeout is not physical realization; wafer yield, test coverage, packaging and system qualification remain.

check.question: Why does a PDK matter in chip design?
options: It replaces functional verification
It connects design rules and models to a particular manufacturing process
It guarantees every die will pass final test
check.explanation: A PDK ties the design abstractions to process constraints, but yield and qualification still require measurement.

science.title: Timing closure boundary
science.explanation: The clock period must cover launch delay, combinational logic, setup time and an uncertainty budget at the declared path boundary.
science.assumptions: A simplified single-clock path; skew, variation, multi-cycle paths and asynchronous crossings need explicit treatment.

lessons.learningObjective: Name the design transformations and closure gates between an architecture contract and a tested die.
lessons.engineeringExample: A 1 GHz target gives a 1 ns period. If clock-to-Q, logic, setup and uncertainty sum to 1.08 ns, the design fails the declared boundary even if its functional simulation is correct.
lessons.evidenceNotes: The sequence is a representative educational flow. Foundry-specific PDK content and proprietary signoff data are not disclosed.

lessons.name: Package and system preserve the contract
lessons.role: Carries chip interfaces through bonding, boards, racks, facilities and runtime services.
lessons.description: The chip is one participant in a larger communication graph. Bumps, interposers, substrates, power delivery, thermal interfaces, host memory, network fabrics and software runtimes determine whether the die can sustain its intended work. A package can pass electrical test yet fail a thermal or mechanical boundary; a rack can contain tested parts yet lack commissioned power or a compatible data path. CRG therefore continues past tapeout to package and system closure, where interface budgets, workload traces, recovery and useful retained output are measured together.

specs.label: Closure boundaries
specs.value: Die, package, board, rack, hall and workload
specs.context: Each boundary has its own units and acceptance test.

specs.label: Useful output
specs.value: Work retained under stated quality, latency and energy targets
specs.context: Busy hardware alone is not the output metric.

interfaces.name: Die/package interfaces
interfaces.signal: Bumps, PHYs, power and thermal paths

interfaces.name: Operating workload
interfaces.signal: Measured throughput, latency, recovery and quality

lessons.tradeoff: Closer integration reduces some communication distance while increasing assembly, thermal, test and replacement coupling.
lessons.whyAI: Large models expose the full chain: HBM traffic, collective links, power conversion, cooling, storage and recovery all shape useful progress.
mechanism: Match die interfaces to package routing, bonding, power and thermal budgets.
Test the package and integrate it on a board with host, memory and I/O paths.
Commission racks, fabric, cooling and facility services at declared boundaries.
Load data and schedule a workload through compiler, runtime and communication paths.
Measure retained work, errors, recovery and quality over the operating interval.
lessons.misconception: A package specification or rack capacity number is not evidence of useful model work without a workload and readiness boundary.

check.question: What does system closure add after tapeout?
options: Only a larger logo
Package, power, cooling, communication, runtime and workload evidence
Nothing, because a simulated chip is already a data center
check.explanation: Useful computation depends on the complete operating path, not just a logical die.

science.title: Useful-work boundary
science.explanation: A bounded accounting model multiplies executed work by a quality/acceptance fraction q and the fraction not lost to interruption or recovery.
science.assumptions: q and f_lost are measured for the declared task and interval; this is not a universal availability equation.

lessons.learningObjective: Trace a chip interface through package and infrastructure boundaries to a retained workload result.
lessons.engineeringExample: A rack can have 64 tested packages yet deliver no useful training step when facility power is uncommissioned, HBM supply is incomplete, or the collective fabric cannot meet the workload’s synchronization bound.
lessons.evidenceNotes: Public product and package pages describe representative boundaries; exact fleet configurations, allocation and service telemetry remain configuration-specific.

lessons.name: The 55-year realization challenge and CRG
lessons.role: Presents Semi AI Foundry’s account of a long-standing computation-to-physical-realization gap.
lessons.description: Semi AI Foundry describes CRG as a framework for closing the distance between computation as an abstract communication process and computation as a manufacturable, verifiable physical system. The company’s article frames this as a challenge that persisted for roughly 55 years before its proposed resolution. In the atlas, that statement is a clearly labeled organizational research claim, not an independently dated historical milestone or a claim that all chip design is solved. The learner can inspect the proposed graph, identify its contracts and tests, and compare the claim with established work on concrete computation, communication and semiconductor design.

specs.label: Claim status
specs.context: Source-dated claim; scope and interpretation remain visible.

specs.label: Historical scope
specs.value: Approximately 55 years, as framed by the source
specs.context: Not converted into a universal chronology without source-specific dates.

interfaces.name: Atlas comparison
interfaces.signal: Explicit boundaries, evidence status and open questions

lessons.tradeoff: A unifying graph can reduce handoff loss while remaining an abstraction that must be tested against actual design, manufacturing and workload evidence.
lessons.whyAI: AGI-scale systems require a sustained path from model intent to physical capacity; CRG gives the atlas a way to teach that path without treating intelligence as detached from machinery.

lessons.scale: Theory, design flow and evidence record
mechanism: Identify the source’s stated gap and preserve its organizational authorship.
Separate the proposed CRG mechanism from independently established technical history.
Map the framework to chip-design, package, system and workload boundaries.
Attach measurable proof obligations rather than treating a diagram as validation.
Record corrections, counterexamples and new evidence as the framework evolves.
lessons.misconception: The CRG claim is not evidence that AGI has been achieved or that undisclosed chip designs are known.

check.question: How should the 55-year statement be used in this atlas?
options: As a dated universal law that replaces semiconductor history
As a source-labeled Semi AI Foundry research claim with explicit scope and open verification
As proof that every future AI system will use one architecture
check.explanation: The atlas preserves provenance and uncertainty while making the proposed realization graph inspectable.

science.title: Claim and evidence separation
science.explanation: A research claim, supporting evidence and an operational qualification decision are different record types. Keeping them separate makes a bold framework teachable without overstating its validation.
science.assumptions: The distinction is epistemic and operational; it does not judge the source’s ultimate correctness.

lessons.learningObjective: Explain the CRG proposal and state exactly what the 55-year claim does and does not establish.
lessons.engineeringExample: Select a model operation and list its representation, interface, timing, energy, error and qualification evidence at each handoff. Missing fields identify an open realization question rather than an invented answer.
lessons.evidenceNotes: Primary source supplied by Semi AI Foundry. The atlas labels this as a research claim and keeps independent technical references beside it.

lessons.name: Verification closes the realization loop
lessons.role: Connects simulation, formal checks, silicon measurement, system qualification and workload evaluation.
lessons.description: A realization graph becomes engineering practice when every edge has a check. Functional simulation and formal methods test logical behavior; timing, power and physical signoff test implementation models; wafer probe, package test and system commissioning test manufactured behavior; workload evaluation tests useful output. These checks have different scopes and failure modes. The loop is intentionally iterative: a measured thermal bottleneck can change placement, package choice, runtime scheduling or even the model’s numerical strategy. The atlas uses this loop to distinguish a plausible design story from an accepted physical system.

specs.label: Evidence ladder
specs.context: Each rung narrows uncertainty at a different boundary.

specs.label: Feedback
specs.context: A failed check is information, not an automatic AGI conclusion.

interfaces.name: Predicted behavior
interfaces.signal: Models, simulation traces and signoff results

interfaces.name: Observed behavior
interfaces.signal: Measured margins, errors, useful work and corrections

lessons.tradeoff: More validation reduces uncertainty but adds time, test structures, instrumentation and cost; the boundary should match consequence.
lessons.whyAI: A model’s capability is only meaningful when computation is correct, capacity is available, failures are recoverable and outcomes meet the declared evaluation task.

sources.title: Semi AI Foundry — Communication Theory of Computation Realization

mechanism: Declare the behavior, metric, unit and acceptance boundary.
Run the least expensive check that can falsify the current assumption.
Move to silicon, package, system and workload measurements as uncertainty narrows.
Track failures to the graph edge and update the affected representation or budget.
Record the qualified scope so evidence is not generalized beyond its task.
lessons.misconception: Passing a benchmark or simulation at one boundary does not qualify every physical or cognitive boundary of the system.

check.question: What is the purpose of the verification loop?
options: To turn an animation into a measurement
To connect predictions and observations across design, manufacturing, system and workload boundaries
To eliminate the need for engineering judgment
check.explanation: Different checks expose different failure modes; the loop preserves scope and feeds corrections back into design.

science.title: Observed margin
science.explanation: A margin is meaningful only when x_observed and x_required share a metric, unit, configuration and time boundary. A negative margin identifies a failed declared condition.
science.assumptions: The scalar margin is a teaching abstraction; multi-dimensional timing, thermal and quality constraints need vector or worst-case treatment.

lessons.learningObjective: Design a scoped verification loop that connects a prediction to an observation and a corrective action.
lessons.engineeringExample: If a package thermal measurement is 82 °C against an 85 °C limit, the margin is +3 °C for that configuration and workload; it is not a fleet-wide guarantee or a model-quality score.
lessons.evidenceNotes: The loop is a systems-engineering teaching pattern. Provider-specific goodput sources illustrate one recovery mechanism, not a universal reliability law.

claims.limitations: This is an organizational research claim, not an independently established universal chronology or proof that all chip realization is solved.
